title: Separate repeatable construction from global state and instance isolation
applies_when: A constructor or alias registration changes shared nodes, global names or configuration-class metadata; independent objects may still consult those globals during lookup or serialization.
lesson: Inspect construction and global readers before choosing a repair. Compare repeated and different-option calls with an ordinary control through the real lookup API. Check that creating a second instance does not change the first. Copying constructor data cannot isolate consumers that still read a global table. Serialization may also read a mutable class attribute even when an instance field stays unchanged: compare an earlier object's to_dict and saved JSON after registering another alias. Also save/reload and check a real alias-sensitive consumer: stable canonical metadata can lose the original model type and change dispatch. Resolve lifetime, class-identity and pickling contracts before introducing dynamic subclasses or removing registration. Confine state loading, file renames and caches to private temporary paths; an in-memory backend does not make the whole constructor side-effect-free.
avoid_when: A one-per-process contract can make independent instances a feature request. A repeated-call failure does not prove a normal one-instance mount fails or a shallow copy is sufficient. Restoring globals after serial tests is isolation, not a concurrent production fix. Distinguish the copied-helper Transformers witness from separately checked full-package get_config on a fixed CPU vLLM wheel; neither qualifies latest-main execution, a repair, serving accuracy or full CI. The JuiceFS sources alone do not establish a supported multi-instance contract. Neither case proves better Scout discovery, PR conversion or cross-framework utility.

evidence.note: NewVFS trims/prefixes global internalNodes, prefixes meta.TrashName, and loads/renames an environment-selected or parent-process-based state file. Source evidence motivates repeat-construction and side-effect controls, not a supported multi-instance contract.
Exported special-name and internal-node lookups consult the shared node table; a constructor-local copy alone cannot provide instance-specific resolution.
Metadata lookup also consumes TrashName. Trace these consumers before treating the VFS node array as the whole ownership boundary.
kimi_k2 and deepseek_v32 map to the same DeepseekV3Config class. _register_config_class changes its model_type before AutoConfig registration. Source mechanism, not full-project validation.

Copied-helper and fixed official e68efc6 CPU full-get_config checks reproduce the mutation. A direct-mapping prototype passed 15 narrow checks but failed six save/reload checks that the original passed; Kimi's real dispatch helper changed selection after alias loss. Prototype rejected. Not latest-main, serving accuracy, an accepted repair or a prospective sample.
